precepts.text: God is talking about the Israelites only. We stumbled wherever we were scattered by following the religions and philosophies of the nations; he will make us walk a straight way. I am a father to Israel, and Israel only: that is what makes us sons of God.
precepts.point: The firstborn receives all the inheritance and the blessings of the father. The covenants, promises and kingdom of God belong to us, joint heirs with Christ.

precepts.text: Israel is my son, even my firstborn.
precepts.point: Their children turned into giants and wickedness, and man's days were cut to 120 years.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Psalm 82 opens: “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” We are the mighty and we are the gods. Then: “How long will ye judge unjustly”? What did we do? Genesis 6:1 tells it: “And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them”. Nations were beginning to form on the earth. Then verse 2 speaks of “the sons of God”.

Who are the sons of God? Exodus 4:22: “And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Now we know who the sons of God are. It is not talking about angels; it is talking about us, before we were called Israel. Before the flood, we were called the sons of God.

“That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” We started taking wives of the other nations, and there were laws on that. Deuteronomy 7:3-4: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”, “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Joshua 23:13 warns that such nations “shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes”. These nations, you marry them, and they are snares and traps unto you. Black women who said the white man is better than the black man were put to death by the men they chose. Sherrone Moore already had a white woman at home, but that was not good enough; he needed a young white woman, and he lost everything for a white coontang. That's a snare and a trap right there. Halle Berry has to pay $8,000 a month to that Edomite, and when she pays him, he says thank you, nigger, and walks away. You can't make this stuff up. Tobit 4:12 says to “take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”, for “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children”.

That was how we judged unjustly and accepted the persons of the wicked. God's son, his firstborn, broke the law he already had, and the Lord said, “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” He cut down our lifespan.

precepts.text: The house of Israel will not hearken unto thee, for they are impudent and hardhearted; fear them not, though they be a rebellious house.
precepts.point: The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Moses answered, “they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice”. Moses knew the spirit of his people, and the word to Ezekiel says it plainly.

“Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them. For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, but to the house of Israel”. Then: “Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee. But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted.”

Israel is impudent, hardhearted and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept. So the Lord made Ezekiel's face strong against their faces: “fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.” That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

precepts.text: Go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.
precepts.point: The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.”

It is the same commission Moses received: go to a people that will not believe and will not hearken, and speak anyway. Ezekiel was to receive all the Lord's words in his heart and go to them of the captivity, whether they would hear or forbear. Israel in captivity today is the same impudent, hardhearted house that Moses knew, and that stubbornness is a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations.

precepts.text: Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds; he had no speech impediment.
precepts.point: The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.” Mighty in words: Moses had no speech impediment.

He did not stutter, as is commonly taught. When he said, “I am not eloquent”, “but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue”, he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language, and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years.

precepts.text: Though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; Paul said the same of himself.
precepts.point: The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Paul said the same of himself: “But though I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been throughly made manifest among you in all things.”

Rude in speech is not a stutter, and neither was Moses being “slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.” Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds; he was simply not fluent in the Hebrew tongue after Pharaoh's house and forty years in Midian. The Lord answered, “I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.”

precepts.text: Every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, for an everlasting covenant; the uncircumcised man child shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
precepts.point: This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
The Lord met Moses in the inn and “sought to kill him” because Moses had not circumcised his son. This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai.

Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” “And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations”, and “my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.”

“And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.” That is why Moses was worthy of death, and why Zipporah had to take a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son herself.

precepts.text: In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised; the law Moses himself later carried to Israel.
precepts.point: This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” This is the law Moses himself later carried to Israel, the same eighth day given to Abraham in Genesis 17.

The man who would carry that law had not kept the covenant with his own son, and the Lord met him by the way in the inn and sought to kill him. Zipporah's sharp stone and her word, “Surely a bloody husband art thou to me”, are what stood between Moses and death.

precepts.text: Abraham was ninety years old and nine when he was circumcised; the covenant is kept at any age.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” He took Ishmael and every male in his house “and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.”

The covenant is kept at any age. A son of Israel must be circumcised on the eighth day; and a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine. The covenant that nearly cost Moses his life still stands.

precepts.text: Paul took Timothy, whose father was a Greek, and circumcised him because of the covenant.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Paul came to Derbe and Lystra and found Timotheus, “the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek”. “Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.”

Paul circumcised Timothy because of the covenant. Timothy came to the truth grown, with a Greek father, and still the covenant of the flesh had to be kept; the same everlasting covenant that the Lord sought to kill Moses over still stands in the New Testament.

precepts.text: After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do; Egypt did not keep the covenant of circumcision.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do”. The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and Egypt did not keep the covenant.

The covenant was between the Lord and Israel. Moses, come out of Egypt, had left his son after the doings of the land of Egypt, and the Lord met him and sought to kill him for it.

precepts.text: There shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth; the unclean do not enter the kingdom.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

Nothing that defileth enters the kingdom; the unclean do not enter. That is why a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty or sixty years, and why the covenant nearly cost Moses his life.

precepts.text: Mortify therefore your members, fornication, uncleanness; for which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: For which things’ sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience”.

Uncleanness brings the wrath of God on the children of disobedience, and nothing that defileth enters the kingdom. Egypt was a nation of uncleanness that did not keep the covenant of circumcision; Israel is not to do after the doings of Egypt, and Moses' uncircumcised son brought the Lord to the inn to kill him.

precepts.text: Circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law; he is a Jew, which is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart; it speaks to lawbreaking, not to ending the covenant of the flesh.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. “For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.” The Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision.

“Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?” The uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised.

“he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter”. This speaks to lawbreaking, not to ending the covenant of the flesh. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say; the covenant that the Lord sought to kill Moses over still stands.

precepts.text: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah; because of the evil of your doings.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.”

This is what circumcision of the heart means in Romans 2: putting away the evil of the doings. It is spoken to the men of Judah, who were circumcised in the flesh; the foreskin of the heart is the evil of their doings, and taking it away is not the ending of the covenant of the flesh that Moses nearly died over.

precepts.text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” Moses himself, who nearly died for not circumcising his son, speaks of the circumcision of the heart to a people already circumcised in the flesh.

The foreskin of the heart is stiffneckedness, the evil of the doings. Circumcision of the heart is putting that away, as the prophets say, and it stands together with the covenant of the flesh, not in place of it.

precepts.text: Ye make clean the outside of the cup, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity; the outward show is not the covenant.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.” “Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.”

The scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within: circumcised in the flesh and breakers of the law, whose circumcision was made uncircumcision. The outward show is not the covenant. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, cleansing first that which is within, and the covenant of the flesh still stands, as it did in the inn when the Lord sought to kill Moses.

precepts.text: Israel is called the Most High's son, even his firstborn.
precepts.point: When Israel was a child, then the Most High loved him, and called his son out of Egypt.

note.label: Hosea 11: When Israel Was a Child

precepts.why: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” Israel is the Most High’s son. Moses was told to say to Pharaoh, “Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. The son called out of Egypt is Israel, his firstborn, whom he loved when Israel was a child.

precepts.text: The Most High sought to kill Moses until Zipporah circumcised her son, because Moses represented God yet had not kept the seal of the covenant.
precepts.point: To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him. Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.”

The Most High sought to kill Moses until Zipporah circumcised her son. Moses represented God, yet he had not kept the seal of the covenant on his own son. “So he let him go.” That shows how seriously the Most High held the token of his covenant.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 22

precepts.why: The firstborn first and foremost goes with Christ, but watch: “Israel is my son, even my firstborn.” The church of the firstborn is Israel, not Moab, not Edom, not Ham, not Ishmael. Only the Israelites.

That is why Moses was worthy of death.

Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people, and the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped. After a long time in which the Lord had not been dealing with them, He finally heard their prayers.
